summary: Jackson County, OR lookout on Anderson Butte; built 1933 or 1935 (sources differ), removed 1965; a 2015 visit found only foundation blocks and a stair pad. Elevation 5,195 ft per the register, 6,193 ft per a survey description on the Forest Lookouts page.

facts.design: 30' L-4 tower per the register and firelookout.com; a 1933 Medford newspaper describes a house atop a thirty-foot tower
facts.elevation_ft: 5,195 per the register (1,583 m); 6,193 per a Coast and Geodetic Survey description quoted on the Forest Lookouts page (see resolved_conflicts)
facts.status_note: Removed in 1965; an April 2015 visit found only the foundation blocks and stair pad

staffing.status: lookout posts through the 1930s-1950s; last post named in 1961

access.note: An April 2015 visit found the access road blocked by dirt berms that stop full-size vehicles, about a mile's walk from the blocked entrance. The sources do not say what the access rules are now.

visit.trail_note: About a mile's walk from the blocked road entrance, per the 2015 visit. No tower remains to climb.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Rogue River National Forest); Southwest Oregon FPA from 1948 per the Forest Lookouts page

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Medford Mail Tribune reports a house on a 30-foot tower, started July 31, 1933 and completed September 12, 1933. Register and firelookout.com date the L-4 tower to 1935. The story gives both.
Register and firelookout.com list the U.S. Forest Service; the Forest Lookouts page says the Rogue River National Forest handed the lookout to the Southwest Oregon FPA in 1948.

Register and firelookout.com give 5,195 ft (1,583 m). A Coast and Geodetic Survey description quoted on the Forest Lookouts page gives 6,193 ft. The story reports the register figure and names the survey figure; the register figure is not confirmed.

notes_for_editor: Build year conflicts (1933 newspaper vs 1935 register and firelookout.com); the story gives both. The only account of the site today is the April 2015 visit reported on the Forest Lookouts page; no later description was found. Brief lists agency as U.S. Forest Service; the 1948 handover appears only on the Forest Lookouts page, so it is a resolved conflict, not a correction. Elevation: the register says 5,195 ft and the Forest Lookouts page quotes a Coast and Geodetic Survey description at 6,193 ft; the story names both. A search snippet cited 5,177 ft (Oregon Field Register); not checked and not used. The register page shows collection photos (1935-1965, 1959, 2015) without image URLs, so no photo entries.
